title: Chipmunks Dance AI: Make the 3-Person TikTok Video From Photos
excerpt: Three photos in, the Chipmunks Dance out: your trio takes turns up front in a vertical 9:16 clip. See what the AI does with each photo and what it costs.
content_html:
Chipmunks Dance AI · 3 photos · 9:16Updated November 2026

Chipmunks Dance AI — Put Your Trio in the Trend

Three photos in, the trio routine out. Your people take turns up front, in a vertical clip with the framing the trend uses. No rehearsal, no finding a day when all three of you are free.

Chipmunks Dance · trio routine · 3 photos

This template maps all three dancers in the opening line-up. For a filmed duo version, split the four handoffs between two people using the steps below.

Independent tool — not affiliated with Bagdasarian Productions, the characters' rights holders, or the recording artists.

Three Things to Know Before You Upload

  • One clear, front-facing photo per person
  • Everyone in the photos is an adult who agreed to this
  • Videos export as clean 9:16 MP4 — no watermark

Make Yours in Three Steps — Chipmunks Dance Video Generator

1. One photo per person

Three uploads, one each: who stands in the middle, who takes the left spot, who takes the right. Front-facing, knees up or full body, even light. No sunglasses, no group shots, no faces turned away.

2. Pick the length, not the choreography

Short covers the opening exchange. Full and Full HD run the whole routine. The routine itself is fixed on purpose — the handoffs land on the same beats every time, which is why a template can reproduce it and a free-form prompt can’t.

3. Download, then add the sound where you post

You get a silent MP4. Attach the track inside TikTok, Reels or Shorts, where the version you’re allowed to use is handled by the platform. That’s deliberate: baking a commercial recording into a file is the fastest way to get a post muted, and it follows you to every repost.

Which Photo Goes Where — Chipmunk Dance AI

This is the only real decision on this page, and it changes the video more than any setting:

  • Middle opens the routine and comes back for a second turn — put whoever wants the spotlight there.
  • Left takes the first changeover: the turn, back to camera, hands behind the head.
  • Right takes the second: wide arm swings, straight at the lens.

The finish is shared. The line closes and everyone moves toward the camera together, so all three photos should be shot at a similar distance and framing — mixing a close-up with a full-body shot is the most common reason a render looks stitched.

Your order stays fixed for the whole clip. If you re-render later, the same photo keeps the same position.

Three People, Two People, or a Full Chipettes Line-Up — Chipmunks AI Video

The trend is built for three. That’s the default here, and the slots are labelled by position instead of by colour, so you’re not forced into one casting.

  • Trio — the standard version: three friends, three siblings, three roommates.
  • Duo — two people instead of three, with the middle and left slots filled and the middle dancer opening and closing. Useful when one of your three is in another city.
  • Right-to-left swap — if your loudest friend belongs on the left, put them there. The template reads positions, not personalities.

Colour is yours to choose. Red, blue and green is the casting everyone recognises, but it isn’t required, and it isn’t something this tool repaints — wear it in the photos and it carries through.

Vertical 9:16 works as-shot on TikTok, Reels and Shorts. Nothing is cropped on upload.

What This Tool Won’t Do

Worth saying plainly, because a lot of chipmunk videos promise it:

  • It won’t animate Alvin, Simon or Theodore. This is a tool for your own photos. Uploading stills of the film characters, or asking for the characters’ faces, isn’t supported and isn’t permitted.
  • It won’t let you upload other people. Only yourself and people who have explicitly agreed. No strangers, no children, no actors from the films.
  • It won’t write the choreography for you. The routine is a template. If you want a different dance, that’s a different template.
  • It doesn’t bundle the recording. Sound comes from the platform’s music library at posting time.

Photos, Permissions, Privacy

Every photo of a person is a permission question before it’s a rendering question. Upload only your own photos and photos of adults who have said yes to this specific video.

Uploads are private, used to render your video, and never used to train models. Deleting your video deletes the source photos with it. Nothing is published anywhere by us — posting is your call, from your own account.

Pricing

Credits, bought once. No subscription, and credits don’t expire.

Packs on this site are Creator, Pro, and Studio. Short, Full, and Full HD use different credit amounts — the generator shows the required credits before you run.

Failed renders return credits automatically to your balance. Unused credit purchases may be refundable within 7 calendar days — see the Refund Policy. Full pack prices are on Pricing.

How many photos do I need?

Three, one per person — the chipmunk dance video generator default. Duo videos use two: fill the middle and left slots; the middle dancer opens and closes.

Which photo should go in the middle?

Whoever should open the routine and come back for a second turn.

How long does it take?

Short renders in a few minutes. Full and Full HD run in two passes and take longer; the page can be closed, and you get an email when it’s done.

Does the video come with the song?

No — the MP4 is silent on purpose. Add the track from the platform’s music library when you post.

Can I post it on TikTok, Reels and Shorts?

Yes. It’s a vertical 9:16 MP4 with no watermark. Switch on the platform’s AI-generated label when you post.

Can I use the video commercially?

For most people this is a personal-post tool. Check our Terms of Service for the licence that applies to your account and use case.

What happens to my photos?

Stored privately, used only for your render, never for model training, and deleted with the video.

Can I do it with two people?

Yes. Fill the middle and left slots; the middle dancer opens and closes.

Is this an official Alvin and the Chipmunks product?

No. Independent tool, not affiliated with the characters’ rights holders, the recording artists, or TikTok.

Trend guide & pricing

This homepage is the product. For the trend history, song, and filmed steps, see the guide on Chipmunks Dance AI.

Independent tool — not affiliated with Bagdasarian Productions, the Chipmunks characters' rights holders, the recording artists, or TikTok.

  • Trio — the standard version: three friends, three siblings, three roommates.
  • Duo — two people instead of three, with the middle and left slots filled and the middle dancer opening and closing. Useful when one of your three is in another city.
  • Right-to-left swap — if your loudest friend belongs on the left, put them there. The template reads positions, not personalities.

Colour is yours to choose. Red, blue and green is the casting everyone recognises, but it isn’t required, and it isn’t something this tool repaints — wear it in the photos and it carries through.

What This Tool Won’t Do

Worth saying plainly, because a lot of chipmunk videos promise it:

  • It won’t animate Alvin, Simon or Theodore. This is a tool for your own photos. Uploading stills of the film characters, or asking for the characters’ faces, isn’t supported and isn’t permitted.
  • It won’t let you upload other people. Only yourself and people who have explicitly agreed. No strangers, no children, no actors from the films.
  • It won’t write the choreography for you. The routine is a template. If you want a different dance, that’s a different template.
  • It doesn’t bundle the recording. Sound comes from the platform’s music library at posting time.

Photos, Permissions, Privacy

Every photo of a person is a permission question before it’s a rendering question. Upload only your own photos and photos of adults who have said yes to this specific video.

Uploads are private, used to render your video, and never used to train models. Deleting your video deletes the source photos with it. Nothing is published anywhere by us — posting is your call, from your own account.
